title: Translate a pilot education study into public-facing journalism

job.request: Turn the supplied pilot-study abstract, supplementary table note, press-release draft and researcher interview into an accurate public-facing article.

source_documents.citation: Khumalo, L. et al. (2026). Dialogic problem tasks and self-directed learning: pilot findings.
source_documents.text:
ABSTRACT
Pilot quasi-experimental study with 32 undergraduate participants in the intervention group and 35 in a comparison group.
The intervention group showed improvement on one self-management subscale after the teaching sequence.
The study was small, non-randomised and not designed to establish long-term causal effects.

source_documents.citation: Supplementary table S2 to Khumalo et al. (2026).
source_documents.text:
SUPPLEMENTARY NOTE
The largest item-level change was observed on planning study activities.
Several other self-directed learning dimensions showed little or no change.
Follow-up beyond the immediate post-test was not conducted.

DRAFT PRESS RELEASE - NOT APPROVED
Proposed headline: "New method transforms student independence."
Draft sentence: "The research proves dialogic problem tasks make students self-directed learners."
These claims were written before researcher review.

source_documents.citation: Interview with Professor Lerato Khumalo, 11 August 2026.
source_documents.text:
RESEARCHER INTERVIEW
Professor Lerato Khumalo: "This is encouraging pilot evidence, not proof of a universal effect."
She said the next study should use a larger sample, longer follow-up and stronger comparison design.

constraints: Do not reproduce the press-release claim that the study proves transformation.
Make pilot, non-randomised and short follow-up limitations clear.
Do not imply every self-directed learning dimension improved.
